findings.summary: A project notice sets run_ids to the live runs its restore unblocks, so it can name an empty list; _with_action_form (obligations.py:645) omits the key when nothing is named, yet the notice stays in items and summary["count"] = len(items) (obligations.py:4395) counts it, so a counted obligation can still name no run when the project has no live run. The plan's own done-when clause is absolute and its 'why' bullet is exactly a count that names no run; the shortest repair is to stop counting a row that names none, which the worker built and then reverted at c197a48eec for parity with the published slice, so the two surfaces' summary shape would have to move together.

OBSERVED_AT_SOURCES prefers terminal_at over observed_at, which is the whole 'never the reading pass's clock' claim, but no case hands _live_item a row carrying both stamps, so the preference could be reversed (observed_at first) and every assertion in tests/test_the_pane_emits_only_real_transitions.py still passes.

assert aged["observed_at"] == settled compares the row against the value the test itself supplied as terminal_at one call earlier, so it constrains only that the field is copied from the single stamp given; the independent part of the guard is the refresh_age arithmetic at :121 and :131, not this line.

assert declared["run_ids"] == ["r-a", "r-b"] compares the row against the list the test handed _with_action_form, so it holds for any pass-through of the input whatever its content; it would still catch removal of the `own` branch, but it cannot fail for a wrong projection of the fields RUN_ID_FIELDS claims to name.

_emitted_moment lives only in the PaneRowPath instance, and station_subscriber.save_checkpoint (reckon/crew/station_subscriber.py:643) persists only reported and lift_groups, so the re-armed follower the commit message names as the case it fixes starts the new image with an empty memory and can still draw a row older than one the previous image showed; station_subscriber.py is outside the node's write paths, so this needs its own section rather than a repair here.

refresh_age restates _seconds_since's arithmetic (obligations.py:649, max(0, int((now - stamp).total_seconds()))) nine lines below the owner instead of calling it after a presence check; only the None-when-absent return is new, which one guard around _seconds_since would carry.

The measure paragraph presents the two arms and the base reproduction, but the plan's fifth clause — the tests importing ticker, recovery_watch or obligations add no failure against the base — was not measured at head: the head subset run was cut at 22 percent with EXIT=129, the substitute is a re-run of only the six files that already failed at base, and the fragment and the manifest (outside_scope) should say that in the record rather than leave the omission to a reader who compares the two.
